h1: AI Product Videos and Photos for Beauty Brands, From One Photo
lead: Shoppers trust a shade they can see in use. One daylight photo of the package becomes a routine, a swatch, or a short review without a studio day.
card: Routines, swatches, unboxings, and short reviews from one beauty photo.
steps_h2: Your Next Beauty Video Ad for TikTok
steps_lead: Three things you do on screen. The rest is checking the shade before you post.

steps.d: Use a straight-on daylight photo with the whole package in frame. Keep the label area visible, and leave hands out of this source shot.
Name one action, such as a pump, a swatch, or an unboxing. If a person is in frame, that presenter is generated, not your customer.
Compare the shade with the real product, then download. Add the price, shade name, or offer in your editor. Captions are not added for you.

faq.q: Can I make beauty ads from one product photo?
faq.a: Yes. Upload a clear, straight-on photo and describe a routine, swatch, unboxing, or review. Compare the shade and the package with the real item before you post.

faq.q: Can I make a before-and-after of skin results?
faq.a: No. A generated face is not evidence of what a product does to skin. Show application, texture, and packaging, and keep result claims out of the ad.

faq.q: Will the clip match my foundation or lipstick shade?
faq.a: Color follows your photo and your wording. Shoot in daylight and name the shade in plain words, such as warm beige liquid. If the tone drifts, make another version. Credits for a failed job come back.

faq.q: Can I put a price or a promo code on the image?
faq.a: Add prices, codes, and product names afterward in your editor. Generated lettering is often wrong, so leave the picture clean.

faq.q: What photo should I upload for skincare?
faq.a: Use a straight-on shot, label toward the camera, on a plain surface, with no hands in frame. Glossy tubes and glass pick up glare, so use window light instead of flash.

faq.q: How long should a beauty ad be, and what does it cost?
faq.a: Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. A 6-second clip is 24 credits, 10 seconds is 40, 15 seconds is 60, and 30 seconds is 120. Use a short length for one pump or swatch.

faq.q: Can I run the clips as paid beauty ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloads are watermark-free and licensed for commercial use, including paid ads. Keep ingredient and result claims accurate, and add text in your editor so you can check it.

faq.q: How is this different from hiring a creator?
faq.a: You upload one photo and pay the credits shown before the job, instead of a creator fee and revision rounds. The person is generated, so present the clip as an ad, not as a customer's review.
